sizeComparison.definition: Extracted bytes=sum of file lengths, excludes allocation overhead/userdata/shared framework. Runtime includes localization.

optimized.policy: cached discovery and bounded receiver backoff

limitations: Synthetic feature replies and immediate synthetic timeouts; no USB latency, real radio traffic or battery drain was measured.
Simulated time advances without sleeping; this is a short software smoke workload, not a 20-minute physical run or endurance test.
CPU, allocations, working/private memory and handles are process-wide before/after observations; other runtime/WPF work and JIT/GC/scheduler noise may contribute.
Memory figures are snapshots, not peak or steady-state memory; CPU/memory deltas are reported without a performance pass threshold.
Legacy is the same managed monitor with efficiency options omitted; optimized uses the new default cache/backoff policy. Healthy refresh cadence is identical.
Policy measurements run sequentially after warmup; query/enumeration counts are deterministic, but one short CPU/memory sample does not establish a causal performance percentage.

presentation.baselineNote: The previous release already cached icon bitmaps and menus. Zero redundant renders/menu creations verifies preservation; selection and shared-DPI probe counts exercise the new reductions.
presentation.limitations: Native property-assignment counters do not trace Shell_NotifyIcon syscalls. Actual USB events and physical mixed-DPI behavior were not exercised.

limits: Normal production apphost/controller/startup, live idle CPU/memory and lazy-popup integration were not run or timed.
Synthetic monitor workload is not startup/idle/physical performance; host changed from embedded app to companion so process snapshots are not a before-after product comparison.
Native styles/hooks/foreground snapshot only; actual game/input routing and physical DPI/power/Explorer/PnP events unverified.
No physical battery/device/endurance testing or new evidence of hardware capacity-health support.
Installer lifecycle uses current app bytes in its earlier-version fixture; no historical-binary migration claim.
No third-party production NuGet dependencies changed; all runtime/localization/license/notice bytes retained.
